findings.title: Sudoers rule gives root to a script the operator can edit, plus wildcard arguments
findings.description: `MT_INSTALL` lets `manta` run `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh --ref *` as root with no password. That script sits in a checkout the `manta` account owns, so `manta` can edit it and then run it as root. The rule is therefore equivalent to full root for that account, which contradicts the header's "nothing wider". `MT_RUN` is `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *` and `MT_UNITS` is `mt-*`, so both accept any arguments. They are only as narrow as `mt-run` and `systemctl` happen to be. `MT_READ` hands over the file that holds the secrets (`/etc/manta-trading.env`). The comment also does not say that the install path is a hard-coded home directory. Fix this by having the sudo rule point at a root-owned copy of the installer, for example under `/usr/local/sbin`, or by documenting the account as fully trusted. Also confirm that `mt-run` validates its arguments.

findings.title: Import ordering violates the required ruff `I` rule
findings.description:
The new names are not in sorted position:
- In `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py`, `NOTES_DIR`, `fire_unit_until` and `start_log` come before `CutoverError`.
- In `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py`, `cagg_freshness_for_session` comes before `CheckReport`.
- In `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py`, the `minute_sessions` and `repair_921` imports come before `gaps.minute_coverage`.
- In `test/unit/test_repair_921.py`, `cagg_freshness_for_session` comes before `SymbolFindings`.

Ruff's isort rule would flag these, and the guide requires `I` to be enabled. Run `ruff check --fix`.

findings.title: Cagg freshness probe can report "fresh" when it is stale
findings.description: `stale` compares `last_successful_finish` with `max(created_at)`. A refresh job that started before the last bars were written but finished after them looks fresh, even though it never materialized those bars. The `job_stats` view also has `last_run_started_at`. Comparing the bar's `created_at` with the refresh's start time is the safe choice. `last_successful_finish` can also be NULL while `last_run_status` shows a failure, and the code reads that as "stale". The retry loop then waits 75 minutes with no explanation. This is an edge case and a narrow one, but the probe is what decides acceptance.

findings.title: Test setup copy-pasted across the new daemon tests
findings.description: `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` repeats about 50 lines of the conn, pool, lock and patch scaffolding that `_run` already builds. `TestTruncatedDayAwareSeeding` repeats it again. Move this into a fixture or helper and parametrize on `(bounds, bars, chunk_end)`. The duplication goes against DRY and the one-concept-per-test guidance, and it will make later changes costly.

findings.title: Stale timer comment
findings.description: The comment says the minute pass is "Staggered 30 minutes behind mt-daily-pass.timer". The daily pass fires at 00:35/12:35, and the minute pass now fires at 04:05/13:05. The stagger is no longer 30 minutes and the first firing is now in a different place. Update the comment and add the reason for the new 04:05 time.

findings.title: Module-level `_LOG_FILE` global in `cutover_common`
findings.description: `start_log` sets a global and `say` appends to it, reopening the file on every call. That is acceptable for an operator script. `start_log` truncates any existing file at the given path, but the timestamped name avoids collisions. Also, `fire_unit_until` prints some narration with plain `print`, so those lines never reach the log file.

findings.title: Session-based chunk judgement and truncated-day seeding
findings.description: The `(open, close]` predicate is a pure function with a narrow `except` that explains why it swallows the error. The unit tests cover the spillover case, the weekend tail, and the boundary bars. The scan-timeout handler logs with `logger.exception` and degrades in a way the comment describes.
